workload.description: 8 GiB of model weights in 512 pages of 16 MiB, cold-loaded through three checkpoint layouts (contiguous safetensors-like sequential page order; 4-shard strided round-robin; mmap-order deterministic random permutation) under three storage/link scenarios. Two policies on the identical page set: (A) demand — synchronous serial NVMe->host->device per page; (B) template pipeline — the recorded access order replayed as a two-channel pipeline (NVMe producer stages into a bounded host RAM window; PCIe consumer streams pages to device), producer gated so staged-but-not-copied pages stay within the window; (C) head pre-warm — the first 128 pages of the learned order staged during the idle window before serving (window = 2 GiB, so the head exactly fills it), remaining pages streamed as in B.

config.layout_nvme_penalty: contiguous = full sequential bandwidth; sharded strided = 1/2; mmap random = 1/4 (configured, not measured)

matched_baselines.description: Demand (serial) vs template pipeline vs head pre-warm + pipeline, identical page set and template order; only the load policy differs. Cold wall = time from 'serve requested' to last page resident on device; pre-warm window runs BEFORE serving and is reported separately.

contiguous.note: pipeline occupancy pins at the 2 GiB budget: the window mechanism demonstrably binds

sharded_x4.note: natural producer lead is 74 pages (1.2 GiB) < 2 GiB budget: the window does NOT bind — the occupancy column reports when host RAM actually fills, not a constant

mmap_random.note: random layout's effective NVMe rate (1/4) makes the producer the bottleneck: consumer drains immediately, occupancy stays at one page

findings.overlap_not_bandwidth: The pipeline buys OVERLAP, not bandwidth: when the storage tier dominates (SATA scenario) the streaming-pipeline win collapses to 1.02x-1.06x; it peaks (1.58x contiguous) when the two channel times are comparable, and in the link-bound scenario the win comes from hiding NVMe reads under the slow device link (1.43x-1.85x).
findings.layout_dwarfs_pipeline: Layout penalties dwarf the pipeline win for mmap-random formats: random access costs 4x NVMe effective bandwidth (configured 1/4 rate), so the cold-load latency across weight formats spans 1.94s-69.79s under demand while the pipeline ratio only varies 1.02x-1.58x. Choosing a contiguous layout matters more than pipelining for random-order formats.
findings.head_prewarm_amortizes_fast: The 2 GiB head pre-warm window breaks even after ONE serving session in every scenario/layout pair measured, because the savings per session (1.02s-18.25s) exceed the window cost (0.31s-17.18s).
findings.window_occupancy_is_measured_not_asserte: The occupancy column shows the window binding only when it must (scenario 3 contiguous: pinned at 128 pages = 2 GiB; sharded: natural 74-page lead under the budget; scenario 1 streaming: 1 page because the consumer drains faster than the producer stages).

metric_honesty.simulation: All rates (7/0.5 GB/s NVMe sequential, 1/2 and 1/4 layout penalties, 12/8/3 GB/s PCIe links, 2 GiB staging) are configured, not measured device numbers; the engine integration must replace them with measured Hanzo-hardware rates.
metric_honesty.recording_stand_in: The template's access order comes from the layout's canonical page order, standing in for a recorded cold-load run; a real PPC/MAIO deployment records the order from an actual load. The replay mechanism is identical either way.
metric_honesty.io_engine_out_of_scope: No io_uring / CUDA staging / mmap syscalls here — this is the template + policy layer with a deterministic recurrence; the actual IO engine is the engine integration follow-up.

hypotheses.text: Pipelining the two transfer channels cuts cold-load wall time whenever neither channel strictly dominates, and the win approaches max(Σread, Σcopy)+startup instead of Σread+Σcopy
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: storage-bound regime (SATA): both policies pay the same Σread, so the win collapses toward 1.0x

hypotheses.text: Checkpoint layout affects absolute cold-load latency through its NVMe access pattern far more than the load policy affects the ratio
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: if page-granular random reads ran at sequential bandwidth, all layouts would share one cold-load latency
hypotheses.observed: confirmed: demand spans 1.94s-69.79s across layouts in scenario 2 while pipeline ratios stay within 1.02x-1.58x

hypotheses.text: A head pre-warm window sized to the staging budget breaks even after a single replayed serving session
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: if per-session savings were below the window cost (e.g., tiny models or one-shot loads), break-even would exceed 1 session
hypotheses.observed: confirmed for this 8 GiB workload: break-even = 1 session in all nine scenario x layout pairs

hypotheses.text: The staging-window gate keeps host occupancy within the budget and the occupancy column honestly reports when it binds
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: an ungated producer would exceed the budget whenever the consumer is slower than the producer
hypotheses.observed: confirmed by test staging_window_bounds_producer_lead and the scenario 3 occupancy columns (128 pinned / 74 natural / 1 drained)

tests.result: cargo test green on windows/amd64, stdlib-only (module); example uses only the module

out_of_scope: the actual IO engine: io_uring/Overlapped I/O, CUDA host staging, mmap syscalls, tensor-level placement
learned predictors beyond replaying a recorded order (template drift / staleness handling)
quantization-aware page sizing and weight-format file formats themselves
multi-model concurrent pre-warm scheduling and eviction of staged templates
real device measurements — configured rates until the Hanzo-hardware rerun

upstream_figures_are_not_hanzo_expectati.ppc_maio_paper: authors report up to 79% model-load latency reduction in their environment (FAST '26)
upstream_figures_are_not_hanzo_expectati.stance: not reproduced on Hanzo hardware; not treated as a Hanzo expectation per the bounty's own caveat. This PR's figures are the only numbers it claims: 1.02x-1.85x streaming-pipeline and 1.35x-2.11x head-pre-warm cold-load improvements on the deterministic workload, with the regime map showing exactly when each wins.

replication: git checkout the PR head; cargo run --release -p hanzo-bench --example load_templates_bench
